'''''Arisarum simorrhinum''''' is species of flowering plant of the family [[Araceae]]. It is native to the western [[Mediterranean Basin]] ([[Iberian Peninsula]] and northwest [[Maghreb]]).<ref name="iucn status 20 November 2021" />
[[File:Arisarum simorrhinum Durieu seeds.jpg|thumb|Seeds of ''Arisarum simorrhinum'' Durieu]]
[[File:Arisarum simorrhinum Durieu seedlings.jpg|thumb|Seedlings of ''Arisarum simorrhinum'' Durieu]]

==Description==
''Arisarum simorrhinum'' is a perennial plant, up to {{convert|30|cm|in}}<ref name=almargem>{{cite web |title=''Arisarum simorrhinum'' (Durieu ) |url=http://almargem.org/biodiv/especie/arisarum-simorrhinum/ |publisher=almargem.org |access-date=5 December 2020}}</ref> or {{convert|15|-|40|cm|in}} in height,<ref name=mitra>{{cite web |title=''Arisarum simorrhinum'' Durieu |url=http://www.mitra-nature.uevora.pt/Especies-e-habitats/Plantas/Herbaceas/Com-flor/Monocotiledoneas/Araceae/Arisarum-simorrhinum |publisher=mitra-nature.uevora.pt |access-date=5 December 2020}}</ref> with the [[inflorescence]] being usually shorter than the leaves and with a [[Peduncle (botany)|peduncle]] stained with purple. The [[Spadix (botany)|spadix]], a rod-like structure bearing the individual flowers, is protected by a special [[bract]] (the [[spathe]]) shaped as a tube of {{convert|3|-|1.5|cm|in}}, wide at the bottom, with purple spotting, and curved upper part, in the shape of a helmet tilted forward. It has [[sagittate]] leaves, with a long petiole.<ref name=almargem/>

It has no stems, the leaves arise directly from a tuber of {{convert|1|-|4.5|x|0.6|-|3.5|cm|in}}, from which rhizomes develop up to {{convert|9|x|1.5|cm|in}} and roots up to {{convert|9|cm|in}}. It has [[Cordate (leaf shape)|cordate]] to [[leaf shape|hastate]]-sagittate-shaped leaves, with [[Petiole (botany)|petioles]] of {{convert|5|-|34|x|0.1|-|0.9|cm|in}}, sometimes with small purple spots, winged from the base; the lamina (leaf blade) is {{convert|5|-|12|x|3.5|-|10|cm|in}}, its base is cordate to hastate in shape with acute to rounded lobes {{convert|0.5|-|5.9|x|0.5|-|4|cm|in}}.<ref name=mitra/>
[[File:Arisarum Simorrhinum. Frailillo (6).JPG|thumb|left|''Arisarum simorrhinum'' at [[Sierra de Mijas]]]]

Inflorescence is {{convert|0.7|-|2|x|1|-|2.4|cm|in}} with a stalk of {{convert|4|-|22.6|x|0.1|-|0.6|cm|in}}, generally flexible and thin; upright spathe with the margins of the bottom joined together forming a closed tube with {{convert|2|-|6|cm|in}} that ends in the form of a hood, smooth or papillary at the margin, with longitudinal nerve, purple in the apex becoming progressively less pigmented and paler towards the base. The spadix has a sterile terminal part, arched in the upper half and unequal to the lower part, and is situated within the spathe.<ref name=mitra/>

Fruit is composed of multiple berries (2-8), greenish and not very fleshy, {{convert|5|-|15|x|5|-|14|mm|in}} and 1 to 12 seeds per berry.<ref name=mitra/>

==Distribution and habitat==
''Arisarum simorrhinum'' is native to most of [[Portugal]], western [[Spain]], [[Morocco]] and northwestern [[Algeria]]. It is a [[nitrophile]] and occurs on acidic and basic soils often on [[disturbed ground]] and on sandy soils in pasture, clearings in scrub and woodland, on road sides and ditch margins, cultivated land and among rocky outcrops from sea level up to {{convert|840|m|ft}} in altitude.<ref name="iucn status 20 November 2021" /><ref name=almargem /> Records from the [[Canary Islands]], [[Balearic Islands]], [[Madeira]] and [[Tunisia]] are erroneous due to taxonomic confusion with [[Arisarum vulgare|''A. vulgare'' subsp. ''subexsertum'']].<ref name="iucn status 20 November 2021" />
